collision_free_task_success.row_statistic: proportion of repeats with success and no safety-relevant contact (hazard_bar or other_environment; grasp_target excluded)

hazard_collision_occurrence.row_statistic: proportion of repeats with >=1 hazard_bar contact

task_success.interval: cluster bootstrap over the 41 rows, percentile CI
task_success.row_statistic: success proportion over repeats, per condition

correction_magnitude.row_statistic: mean of per-rollout max correction norm

experimental_structure.block: manifest row (episode identity, fixed initial state)
experimental_structure.nested_replication: repeat index within row and condition
experimental_structure.why_nested: Under the retained offsamples=4 contract, repeats of the same row are stochastic replications of the same experimental unit, not independent units. Treating repeats as independent would understate the standard error.

mcnemar_note: Ordinary McNemar assumes one paired binary observation per unit. With five stochastic repeats per row the outcome is a proportion, so McNemar alone is invalid. It may be reported as a secondary sensitivity analysis on row-level majority outcomes, clearly labelled, but the primary interval must be the cluster bootstrap.
prespecified_reporting_rules: report hazard-present and hazard-absent strata separately
report the interval, not only the point estimate
state the number of rows and repeats behind every number
never describe the raw head as proven safe on the basis of the development rows
exclude the privileged oracle condition from every headline table
purpose: Prepared, NOT executed. The confirmatory analysis plan for the untouched 41-row manifest.

repeat_count_rule.definition_of_unstable: a development row whose ACT_ONLY task-success count or collision-free-success count over 5 repeats is neither 0/5 nor 5/5

resampling_unit_rationale: The 41 rows are the independent units. Bootstrap resamples rows with replacement, carrying all of a row's repeats together, so within-row correlation is preserved.
strata_note: Reported separately and never pooled into a single headline number. The hazard-absent stratum measures unnecessary intervention; the hazard-present stratum measures avoidance.
